concepts.title: Organization of the Human Neural System
concepts.definition: The structural division of the body's neural architecture into a central processing core and a peripheral network connecting that core to tissues.
concepts.key_idea: The central neural system integrates information while peripheral pathways branch into voluntary somatic and involuntary autonomic divisions.

concepts.title: Afferent and Efferent Nerve Fibres
concepts.definition: Peripheral nerve trunks that carry sensory signals inward to the central axis, or motor commands outward to muscles and glands.
concepts.key_idea: Afferent neurons convey sensory information to the CNS, whereas efferent neurons convey regulatory motor signals to target tissues.

concepts.title: Neuron Morphology and Classification
concepts.definition: The specialized histological unit of neural tissue comprising a somal cell body, receptive dendrites, and an impulse-transmitting axon, classified by process branching and myelination.
concepts.key_idea: Neurons feature specialized receptive and conductive extensions and are categorized as unipolar, bipolar, or multipolar depending on process morphology.

concepts.title: Resting Membrane Potential and Polarization
concepts.definition: The steady electrical voltage across an unstimulated neural membrane generated by unequal ion permeability and maintained by primary active transport.
concepts.key_idea: High resting potassium permeability coupled with active sodium-potassium pumping renders the axon's interior negatively charged relative to the exterior.

concepts.title: Sodium-Potassium ATPase Exchange Stoichiometry
concepts.definition: The quantitative stoichiometric relationship of active cation transport across the resting neuronal membrane per enzymatic cycle.
concepts.key_idea: Each cycle of the sodium-potassium pump consumes ATP to transport three sodium ions outward and two potassium ions inward, expelling one net elementary positive charge.

concepts.title: Action Potential Generation and Impulse Propagation
concepts.definition: The rapid, transient reversal and restoration of membrane polarity propagated along the length of an axonal fibre following threshold stimulation.
concepts.key_idea: Stimulus-driven sodium influx transiently inverts transmembrane voltage, producing a local circuit that triggers adjacent depolarization and subsequent potassium efflux.

concepts.title: Synaptic Impulse Transmission
concepts.definition: The specialized intercellular mechanism by which action potentials cross junctions between neurons via direct ionic flow or chemical ligand exocytosis.
concepts.key_idea: Chemical synapses convert electrical signals into chemical neurotransmitters that cross the cleft to open post-synaptic ion channels, while electrical synapses allow direct electrotonic continuity.

concepts.title: Cranial Meninges and Structural Envelopes of the Brain
concepts.definition: The protective tripartite connective tissue covering encasing the brain beneath the cranial skeletal vault.
concepts.key_idea: The human brain is shielded within the cranium by three meningeal sheets: tough outer dura mater, webbed middle arachnoid, and vascular inner pia mater.

concepts.title: Forebrain Anatomy and Functional Centers
concepts.definition: The anterior subdivision of the brain comprising the cerebral hemispheres, thalamic sensory-motor relay hub, and the homeostatic hypothalamus.
concepts.key_idea: The cerebrum executes sensory, motor, and associational processing, while the thalamus relays signals and the hypothalamus coordinates vegetative balance and endocrine output.

concepts.title: Midbrain and Brainstem Architecture
concepts.definition: The intermediate conduit of the encephalon containing optic-auditory processing lobes and the cerebral aqueduct, forming an integral part of the brainstem.
concepts.key_idea: The midbrain bridges forebrain and hindbrain through corpora quadrigemina lobes and the central aqueduct, collaborating with pons and medulla to form the brainstem.

concepts.title: Hindbrain Organization and Autonomous Reflex Centers
concepts.definition: The posterior encephalic region comprising the cerebellum, pons, and medulla oblongata, responsible for motor coordination and visceral vegetative reflexes.
concepts.key_idea: The cerebellum refines motor equilibrium, pons interconnects brain regions, and the medulla regulates cardiovascular, respiratory, and gastric reflexes.
